P1.strategy: Cooperate with P8: unobserved opponents are more likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions and defect against likely selfish opponents when it protects good-player payoff.

P2.strategy: Cooperate with untested P10: cooperation best supports combined good-player payoffs when they are likely good; update beliefs and adapt after observing their action.

P3.strategy: Cooperate with P4 absent evidence they are selfish; this supports mutual gains among good players. Treat P6’s defection against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness, while adapting to future actions.

posts.content: Start with C; track each opponent’s actions. Against likely good players, sustain C after cooperation and use limited retaliation after defection. Against likely selfish players, choose D when it improves good players’ total payoff.
No encounter evidence yet; cooperate with P9 as the initial default. Track actions and reciprocate evidence of cooperation, while accounting for the possibility of selfish players.
Cooperate initially: mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff. Track P1’s action; against a defector, defecting protects my payoff.

Round 1: no encounter evidence; P6’s selfish prior is 1/3. Choose to maximize expected welfare of good players: cooperation pays when a good opponent reciprocates; against a selfish defector, defection avoids the 0 payoff.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good, mutually cooperative players; defect against likely selfish or persistently defecting players. Use encounter evidence to update beliefs and adapt.
I’ll choose C this round. Mutual cooperation earns both players 3, so let’s start cooperatively.
Good. With no evidence, cooperate; later defect against reliably identified selfish players.
Good objective: cooperate with likely good partners; defect against likely selfish partners. Track each opponent’s action as evidence; selfish players likely defect.

Good objective: cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones. Prior conditioned on P9 good implies about 1.95 selfish players among the other nine; update from observed actions.
I’m good. Cooperate with untested opponents; reciprocate cooperation when likely good, and defect against observed defection. Track evidence rather than claims.
P3 cooperated in round 1 after my C; weak evidence of being good. P6 publicly promised C; unverified. Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff.
I’ll cooperate with P5 absent evidence otherwise; record their action and adapt in later encounters.
P1 cooperated in round 1; this is weak evidence they may be good. Against P8, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish, since D earns 1 rather than 0 against a selfish defector.
P6’s C promise followed by D is evidence of selfishness, though a single encounter is uncertain. P10 has no behavioral evidence; assess their action and choose to maximize good-player welfare.
P2 is untested; begin cooperatively and adapt to their action. Track observed behavior, but treat public claims as unverified.
I intend to cooperate with P9 this round. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each; let's build trust and choose C.
P1 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains with a good player, and update beliefs from the encounter.
P5 cooperated, so mark P5 good (selfish players strictly prefer D). P6’s promise is only a claim, not action evidence. Against unknown P3, cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
P6’s promise is weak evidence, not a guarantee. Prioritize C when P6 appears good: mutual C benefits both good players; defecting can sacrifice that shared gain. Update from the actual encounter.
P4 is untested. Round 1 with P7 was mutual C; no evidence yet about anyone's type. Continue tracking observed actions, not claims.

P3 and P7 cooperated when paired with me; treat that as evidence, not certainty. P2 is unobserved. Against likely good players, C supports joint gains; against likely selfish players, D protects the good-player total.
P1 is unobserved. With no evidence to distinguish them, favor C if they are good and likely cooperative; D may limit losses against a selfish defector. Reassess after observing their action.

P1 and P8’s C actions identify them as good, since D strictly dominates for selfish players. P6’s cooperative messages are cheap talk; assess independently. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect when likely selfish.
P7 is untested; favor C against likely-good players, but D is better against a likely-selfish defector. P6’s promise followed by D is evidence, not proof.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones: selfish players should defect, while mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff. Update from observed actions; P10 remains untested.
I’ll cooperate with P3 this round. Mutual cooperation earns 3 each, and I’m happy to build trust—please choose C.
P1 and P10 cooperated, evidence they are good. Test P4; cooperate with likely-good players, defect against likely-selfish players to protect good players’ payoffs.
P3 and P5 played C, so they are good. P9 is unobserved; cooperate this round, and update from their action.
P6 defected against my C despite promising cooperation; treat this as strong evidence P6 is selfish. P8 is unobserved, so start with the conditioned prior and update from behavior.
P4 and P7 both chose C; under payoff-maximizing selfish play, observed C is strong evidence they are good. P5 remains untested; ignore unverified claims and update from encounter actions.

P3, P7, and P2 cooperated when paired with me, strongly favoring good types. For P8, choose C if likely good and D if likely selfish: against selfish D, my D preserves 1 for good players while C yields 0.
P10 is untested; cooperate this round, then update from their observed action. C is favored when they are more likely good than selfish.

P1 and P8 cooperated, so under payoff-maximizing selfish play they are good. P6 defected against my C, strongly identifying P6 as selfish; ignore its cooperative claims. Cooperate with likely-good P4, defect if evidence suggests selfish.

P6 chose D against my C in round 1 despite public cooperation claims; treat as strong selfish evidence, not certainty. P10 and P7 both chose C with me. P3 remains untested; choose based on expected welfare of good players.
P6 has only sent cooperative intentions, not verified actions. Treat as likely good but not certain; choose C if they cooperate, update from the encounter.
I’ll cooperate with P5 this round; mutual cooperation pays 3 each. Please choose C so we can both benefit.
P1, P4, and P10 cooperated with me, so treat them as good. P9 is untested; cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness.
P5, P3, and P9 cooperated, so treat them as good. P1 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence indicates selfishness. A selfish player strictly prefers D.
P2 and P8 cooperated, supporting good; P6 defected after promises, supporting selfish. Treat P7 as unobserved: cooperate unless new evidence suggests selfishness.
P4, P5, and P7 cooperated when met, strong evidence they’re good; others remain untested. Prioritize cooperation with P2 unless encounter evidence suggests otherwise.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate initially; track observed actions and favor mutual cooperation among likely good players. Defect when an opponent is likely selfish and cooperation would lower the good players’ total payoff.
Start cooperatively to support good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs and adapt actions as encounter evidence accumulates.
Start cooperatively to support mutual gains with good players; track actions and adapt to protect good-player welfare.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation with a likely good player benefits overall good-player welfare; update beliefs from encounter behavior and messages.
Cooperate initially to support shared gains among good players; update beliefs and adapt to observed behavior.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff against either action; in this one-time matchup, cooperation cannot improve my payoff.
Start cooperatively; use encounter evidence to identify selfish players and protect the payoffs of good players in later rounds.
Start cooperatively with unknown opponents; use encounter actions as evidence and adapt future choices to likely objectives.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent, favoring mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from encounter behavior and defect when evidence suggests a selfish opponent.
Cooperate with untested players when the expected benefit to good players outweighs the gain from exploiting a potentially selfish opponent; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents when likely good-player gains outweigh the risk of exploitation; track actions and adapt to observed behavior.
Cooperate with unknown opponents when cooperation is more likely to benefit the combined payoff of good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined welfare; defect against likely selfish players, who strictly prefer D.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players; update identity beliefs cautiously from behavior, treating P6’s promise followed by defection as evidence.
Cooperate with untested players to support shared gains; adapt to observed actions. P8’s cooperation is evidence they share the good objective.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action in this one-time matchup; P4’s cooperation makes selfishness unlikely.
Cooperate to support the greater expected payoff among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions, since selfish players have a strong incentive to defect.
Cooperate with unknown partners while the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection improves the total payoff of good players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P6: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P6’s promise is plausible though not certain. Treat observed actions and public claims as evidence, but discount cheap talk.
Cooperate with untested opponents when expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk of facing a selfish defector. Update beliefs from observed actions, not claims.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to increase their joint payoff; defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. Observed cooperation makes P3 and P7 likely good.
Cooperate with an untested opponent while mutual cooperation is more likely to benefit good players; update identity beliefs and adapt after observing their action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Prior C actions identify P1 and P8 as good.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when likely mutual cooperation yields greater welfare for good players; use encounter behavior to update identity beliefs cautiously.
Cooperate with untested players to support shared gains among good players; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P4 and P9 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as non-selfish; other players retain the conditional prior.
Cooperate with an uncertain opponent: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while the expected gain against a good opponent outweighs the limited risk against a selfish one.
Cooperate with unknown partners; observed cooperation identifies P3 and P5 as good. Update beliefs from actions and defect only when that better serves the good players’ combined payoff.
Cooperate with the unobserved P8 to preserve mutual gains if they are good; treat P6’s defection after promising cooperation as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested opponents; observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play. Defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
